The main process keeps menus, the tray, window creation, and native dialogs responsive, and the sync workload would block it. `node:sqlite` is synchronous, so a catch-up batch writing several thousand rows holds the thread until it finishes. In main, that shows up as the whole app freezing. Full-text search has the same problem: a query across a large corpus has no useful upper bound on how long it takes (`docs/DESIGN.md:306-315`).

A separate process also isolates crashes. If the sync engine hangs or throws on a malformed frame, it can be restarted without killing the app or closing the user's windows (`docs/DESIGN.md:317-319`). Renderers don't route reads through main either. After the initial handshake they talk to the engine over a direct `MessageChannelMain` port, so main never becomes a proxy on the busiest path (`docs/DESIGN.md:321-325`).
